identification: Soenneker.Email.Mime 11.0.605, configurable MailKit SMTP and MIME utility
scope: Static reverse engineering of every managed method and package member; no sample code executed.
decisive_diff: Fetched original NuGet Soenneker.Email.Mime 11.0.604 with forager; identity/version confirmed from nuspec. Provenance files remain in scratch/mime-drift/previous.
Both MIME assemblies have 33 MethodDef entries (30 bodies and 3 abstract interface methods). Resolved IL, signatures, constants, branch targets and exception handlers are identical.
Nuspec changes: 11.0.604 to 11.0.605, release note and repository commit; Soenneker.Extensions.Stream dependency changes 4.0.173 to 11.0.174. Other dependencies are unchanged.
Fetched both stream dependency releases with forager. The dependency target changes net10.0 to net11.0; resolved method IL and exception handlers are identical.

Remaining changed members are build/version/provenance data and package signature. README, XML documentation, license and icon are byte-identical. No new executable or install/build hook is introduced.
The immediate previous release also has 0 hostile / 1 suspicious trait with current rules, contradicting an interpretation that this version introduced the bypass.
execution_paths: Constructor reads Smtp:Enable and connection settings from IConfiguration. AcceptAnyCert and LogContent use a generated Boolean configuration binder with a false default.

Send returns without delivery if disabled; otherwise a Kevlar retry wrapper calls InternalSend. Retry covers I/O/socket/timeout/protocol and 4xx SMTP failures, with five exponential-backoff/jitter retries.

InternalSend creates a MailKit SmtpClient. At IL 0x7b-0xa8 in its MoveNext, _acceptAnyCert gates construction/installation of RemoteCertificateValidationCallback. The exact target method (MethodDef 0x19) is ldc.i4.1; ret. This accurately establishes an available TLS-validation bypass.

TLS mode is selected from UseSsl and UseStartTls; ConnectAsync receives configured host/port, AuthenticateAsync receives configured SMTP credentials, SendAsync receives the caller-supplied MimeMessage. Disconnect and Dispose follow.

Only with LogContent and debug logging enabled does MIME serialization write the supplied message to a reusable memory stream, rewind it, read UTF-8 text and log it. This is documented optional content logging, not covert network exfiltration.

Generated configuration binders, enum attributes and async state machines explain generated names. No runtime decryption, staged executable, arbitrary process launch, credential-store access, persistence or C2 path occurs in the recovered bodies.
context_limits: Caller settings, messages, logging destination and actual deployment authorization are unavailable. No production enabling of AcceptAnyCert is assumed. Declared author/repository are provenance claims, not signature verification.
